We have limited the exhibit that we were introducing into evidence based upon the parts that we cross-examined the witness upon, so I believe it is proper, and I believe that the information elicited is of great benefit to these proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, as has been the case all along, this statement insofar as that -- it has been the subject of the evidence it will form part of the record. It's been used so far only to put in context questions that were asked of the witness in cross-examination, and the parts of the statement referred to are a necessary element of our consideration of the witness's response in due course. So subject to other submissions that may well be made at a later stage about the extent to which we can take account of it, it is for the moment and will continue to be part of the record in the case to the extent it's been referred to.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Marcussen, the paragraphs of the indictment, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour, I was running to get my papers. The paragraphs of the indictment are paragraphs 72(d), 75(d), Schedule D, and paragraph 77. I think we put 77(d) on our witness notification, it's rather 77(a) and (b), or paragraph 77 in general. As another preliminary thing while we wait for the witness, I would like to mention to the Court that this witness is one of those witnesses who has given a statement to the OSCE. There has been an issue in the context of Your Honour's decision on Under Orders and whether or not it was possible to assess the reliability of the underlying evidence for the report. I mention this because this is one of those witnesses where it is possible to -- to compare the underlying information report made by OSCE with the evidence of the witness. We're not intending to tender the -- the information report at this stage, but I would like to draw Your Honours' attention to the exhibit number nonetheless, and the exhibit is P2289. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So you don't actually intend to explore the consistency between the two?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Not at this stage. I think today we will get the evidence from the witness and -- I'm saying it in case --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just bring the witness in, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I'm simply mentioning it in case Your Honours had anything that Your Honours wanted to explore in this regard. I don't know to what extent you had a chance to look at this kind of material. So at this stage, I'm alerting Your Honours to it. We might be making submissions on this later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Good morning, Ms. Berisha.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Would you please make the solemn declaration to tell the truth by reading aloud the document which is now before you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated. Mr. Marcussen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Good morning, Madam Berisha.

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Madam Berisha, what ethnic group do you belong to?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: I'm Albanian.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Do you speak Serbian?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Do you speak any other languages?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Could we --

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: You do -- you do speak Albanian, do you?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes, of course. I speak my own language, Albanian.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I would like if we could see Exhibit P117, page 8. And I believe there are two images on that exhibit, and I'd like to see the top one. Could we zoom in on the top -- on the top one? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Madam Berisha, do you recognise this house?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes. This is the house where I used to live with my husband and with my husband's nephew Faton.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: In what part of the house did you live?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: With my husband and my four children, I lived on the left side of the house, while my husband's nephew Faton and his wife and two children, his mother and his sister lived on the right-hand side of the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Madam Berisha, there will be a lot of names mentioned during your testimony today, so before we continue with the events you are here to talk about, I'd like to ask you if during your meetings with the Prosecution before you testified today, whether you were shown a family-tree for parts of the Berisha family -- sorry, for different Berisha families, I should say?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And on that family-tree, did you verify it to see whether it was correct, according to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And did you indicate that there were some of the people on the family-tree whose name you knew and there were other people who you did not know the name of?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And did you together with one of the OTP investigators mark on a copy of the family-tree the names -- the persons whose name you knew?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Were you also asked to indicate who of the people on the family-tree were in -- were with you in the coffee shop on the day we're going to discuss later?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And was that also marked on -- on a copy of the family-tree by the investigator?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And did you also indicate on the family-tree which family members you knew had been killed in Suva Reka at --

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Madam Berisha, were you then later shown a new copy of the family-tree which incorporated the information you had given to the Prosecution's investigator?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And did you sign and date that copy?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Madam Berisha, I'd like to show you a copy of the family-tree.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I will need the assistance of the usher for that. Your Honours, the family-tree is in e-court and we will be asking that it's tendered as an exhibit. Because of its size, I will not be attempting to show it on the monitor in court. The exhibit number will be P2346.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Madam Berisha, is this a copy of the document that you signed?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And your signature is in the bottom right-hand corner. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this stage I would like to tender Exhibit P2346.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: The Defence should have been given a copy of the exhibit and Your Honours should have received a copy. I believe a look around the room just to see that. That seems to be the case. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Madam Berisha --

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: If we could show -- could we show the Exhibit P117, page 8, the top -- the one we just had before? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: So, Madam Berisha, you say you lived with your husband and four children on the left-hand side of the house that is shown on the monitor now. Could you tell us the name of your --

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Would you tell us the name of your husband and children, please.

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: My husband's name was Nexhat Berisha. The oldest daughter, her name was Majlinda, she was 16. Herolinda, my second daughter, she was 13. Altin, he was 11 years old. And little Redon, he was only 18 months old.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And on the right-hand side of the house on this picture, who lived there?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: My sister-in-law, she was 48 years old, her name was Fatime Berisha. My husband's nephew, Faton Berisha, 28 years old. His wife, Faton's wife, Sebahate was her name, she was 25 years old. Faton's sister, Sherine, 17 years old. And Faton's two sons, Ismet, who was 3 years old, and Eron who was only 10 months old.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And your mother-in-law and Faton and Sebahate's family, they are seen on the family-tree, I think, on the top --

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: -- quarter on the left side of the family-tree. There's also the mention of Arben Berisha. Did he live in the house?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: He was at that time in Switzerland. He wasn't in the house. He's brother -- Faton's brother.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And Ismet at the time that we're going to talk about, was he in the house?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Ismet is Fatime's husband. He died ten years before the war started, while the little Ismet, he is -- he was Faton's son. He was carrying the name of Faton's father. So the senior one, Ismet, he was already dead. He had passed away ten years earlier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, the -- just to be clear about the legend for this, what's the significance of the square and the round boxes?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Square are male and round boxes are female.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Oh. And how do we know which may be deceased prior to the relevant date, such as Ismet that we've just heard of?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: The persons that are indicated in -- in blue and red were all involved in the incident that we are going to talk about later today. All those with a colour are dead with the exception of the witness and two other persons indicated on the family-tree, and I will make sure that the record is clear in that regard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But what's the significance of the names that are written in black?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: They are -- they are the names of family members that the witness knows but they were not present at the coffee shop and have not been -- or were not killed earlier that same day. The reason why we have done it this way is that there are other parts of the family, as can be seen, all the ones that are not in a bolded box, and those are parts of the family that the witness has indicated that she generally knows but she's not able to place them with their name in the family-tree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But can we take it that a number of the names in black may well have been deceased before the event we're talking about?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Some might have died before and there might also be some of those in black who died on that day but who the witness is not able to identify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Could we scroll down, please, to the lower part of the second photograph on this exhibit, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Madam Berisha, are you able to recognise what this picture is?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: This is the back part of the house, it's the back entrance on the other side.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you. Did -- when the OSCE arrived in Suva Reka, do you know where they had their office at the time they came to Suva Reka?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: When they came to Suhareke, their offices were at Hotel Boss and in Shiroka of Suhareke. The owner of that was Miskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Do you know the first name of Miskovic?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: I don't know what his first name is. I just know that he was always called Miskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Did the OSCE later move to your house?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes. At the end of 1998, OSCE moved to our house, but I'm not sure of the exact date when they moved in.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And I'd like to ask that we scroll back up to the top photo -- part of the exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: How did OSCE use the house that we see on the picture? What were they -- what were they using the left-hand side or your part of the house for?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: The OSCE used our house as their offices; while the other part, Faton's part, they lived there. They used it as sleeping quarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Do you know whether there were OSCE staff sleeping in houses -- other houses in Suva Reka?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes, there were people from the OSCE living -- sleeping in other houses. The only house that they used as an office was our house.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Where did you stay when the OSCE moved into your house?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: When OSCE moved in my house, I stayed at my parents, which was in the Mushtisht village, which is about 9 kilometres away from Suhareke.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And where did Faton's family go?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Faton's family stayed with his grandfathers, which -- the house of whom was a little bit further away at the entrance of Suhareke.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: While OSCE was using your house, did you come to the house from time to time?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Two or three times a week. We had to clean the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: While my husband was there every day.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: So did you know the staff working there? I'm thinking in particular of some of the people who provided security for the OSCE mission.

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes, I knew many of them. I can't remember the names now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: I know only that the head was called Rufus. I knew some of the other's names as well, but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you. That's fine. When did the OSCE leave?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: The OSCE left the house in March, but I am not sure about the exact date. Whether it was before the 20th of March or on the 20th of March, I forget, but it was in March.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you. And did you then move back to the house?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes, after they left I went back home -- not my own home. I went to Fatime's house, my sister-in-law's house, which was the other part of the house. That's where we stayed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Had -- had Fatime and Faton's family already moved back at that point in time?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes, they had returned earlier because the people who were sleeping there had left earlier and went and stayed somewhere else. So Fatime and Faton returned to their home earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: When the OSCE left, did they leave any equipment in your house?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And when you came back, were there also still some of the OSCE security people there?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Did you speak to any of them?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes. Once I approached them, I went to the house because I knew that they had left and wanted to clean the house. But as I went to the house there was a guard there. He was a Roma. His name was Zeqa from Suhareke, and he told me: Nexhat's wife, if you -- if the police come, if the Serbian police come, don't fear because they've been here already two times.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Did --

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Did he say why the police had been coming?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: He said that the Serbian police had come to see whether we were being harassed by the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Did you -- do you think that was the real reason?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: No. This was not the real reason because there was no KLA there. I never saw any KLA there. My opinion is that they had gone there to see whether we had returned to our home.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Do you know whether the police visited any of the places where other OSCE staff had been living in Suva Reka?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes. I don't know what days it was. My husband told me that the Serbian police had gone into Murat Suka's house where the OSCE used to use as sleeping quarters. He had heard that the Serbian police had gone in and looted, had taken everything that they had found in there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you. The day that the bombing -- the NATO bombing started, do you remember that day?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: I can't tell you the date now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Did you notice any particular movement of troops that day?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes. There was a lot of movement of the army, the police. The street was full of cars and tanks and policemen and soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Now, the people you describe as soldiers, can you describe what they were wearing?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: As far as I remember there were many buses, and these people were wearing uniforms. They were shouting. There were other buses where people seemed more serious there. They were still in uniforms, but they were more serious, looked more serious. But there were others who were shouting, were firing their guns. They had bandannas on their heads. My son, Altin, who was 11 years old and my -- I remember my son saying to me: Mom, they look like ninjas.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Do you remember the colour of the clothes of the people who were screaming and yelling and shooting in the air?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes. All of them had uniforms. They -- some of them had camouflage uniforms --

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Green, solid colour. Most of them were green uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: You also said that you saw police -- a lot of police move. What kind of uniform were the people you think were the police wear?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes, blue uniforms, camouflage blue uniforms, I would say dark blue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: You mention that you saw people in buses that were very agitated and then there were other people that were more calm. The people that were more calm, how did they look, what were they wearing?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: They, too, had uniforms on, and their hats and uniforms were the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Could we see Exhibit 189, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Madam Berisha, do you recognise this place?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: There are some numbers and markings on this exhibit. Is -- are they markings that were made by one of the Prosecution's investigators who spoke to you?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Now, is it correct that number 1 is your house?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Now, where were the buses and the peoples -- people you just described approximately on this map?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Here on the street.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: On the road to Pristina. On the road here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Is that the lower road? There seems to be two, one running in front of the house and another one running further down. You're describing the lower one. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes. This road here which takes you to the police station and then to Pristina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: It is the lower road being indicated just so the record is clear on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Okay. Madam Berisha, on the next day, the day after the NATO bombing had started, did the police come to your house -- did the police come to your house?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: The policemen came to our house on the 25th of March in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Who opened the door for the police?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: They pushed the door. They knocked at the door very heavily. It was very early in the morning. I'm not sure now whether it was 5.00 a.m. or when, but it was me who opened the door.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: How many policemen did you see?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Three.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Could you describe for me how they looked. Now, first what kind of a -- were they wearing a uniform?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: I'm not sure whether I remember correctly, but I think they had camouflage uniforms, green uniforms, and one of them was wearing this white band on his arm.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: You say they were the police. Why do you think they were the police?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: That's what I thought. They had a uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Did they say why they had come?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: When I opened the door, there was this very tall policeman, the other two were shorter. And the tall one pointed his automatic gun at my chest and asked for my husband.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Did your husband come?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes. I called my husband. He came downstairs and they took my husband and they went to the left side of the house, our house, where the OSCE had its offices.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And when they were in your part of the house, do you know where they went?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: I did not see them because I stayed inside. They did not allow me to go outside. They told me to stay inside. They only took my husband there, and my husband told me what had happened. They took my husband. They asked him about the OSCE. When the policeman found the photographs of the burned villages that the OSCE had taken, they had beaten my husband with chairs, with the butts of their guns, they had kicked him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Did they -- did the policemen -- did your husband tell you whether the policemen entered any of the rooms that had been used by OSCE?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: When the policemen had been searching in their cupboards and cabinets, there were two rooms that were locked and they had broken into those rooms and had threatened my husband, telling him: Where are your Americans? You asked for their help. Where is your father Clinton? And they had offended him with other words. And that's when he told me they had beaten him with the chairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Did -- did they -- apart from the photographs, did the police find anything else?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: He said that when the police broke the door into one of the room, they had found helmets and bullet-proof vests of the OSCE. And my husband told me: It was there that they beat me up the most.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Okay. Did -- did the police also come to the side of the house where you were?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: I was in the house when they took my husband, and in the meantime a policeman came. He was young, and he came to me. Upstairs on the first floor, we were all of us there, the children, Faton's wife, Fatoni. They -- He started searching the cupboards, and I told him: There's nothing in there, it's just children's clothes. And while he was leaving, he found a small bag. It was Sebahate's bag. He took that bag and searched it. And when he saw that there was nothing in that bag, he threw it away. It was just medicine that he found in there. And he beckoned to me: Come to this basement. And when I went to the basement he made this gesture: Do you have any money because your husband is at risk? So I went upstairs. I took a thousand Deutschemarks from Sebahate and went to the basement and gave the money to him. But he said: This is not enough for your husband's life. You have to give me more. I told him: This is all I have. And he went out. I remained in the corridor of the house. In the meantime, I was trying to have a look what was going on in the courtyard, and a policeman came. He had several knives on his chest. He was older. He had a very aggressive face, and he started to run towards me and said: Oh, let me have a look at this woman, how good-looking she is. It was said in a very provocative way. I was so scared, very frightened of him. He was bare-chested, unbuttoned, and he had these knives on his chest. But this other policeman that I gave the thousand Deutschemarks to, he ran off to him and said: Zarko, Zarko, wait. I think even if he came two steps further he would catch me, he would be able to catch me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: What did you do after that?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: So he took that policeman away. I sat down. I was so scared. I don't know how I did not faint. And then the three policemen who took my husband -- so the three policemen who took my husband, they brought him back. And when they were at the door, they hit him and swore at him. Things like: The Americans, your Americans that you have asked for assistance from them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Did you see your husband being beaten?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: It was right in front of my eyes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And it was -- it was the policemen you had seen earlier in the day, the people you describe as policemen who were beating him?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes, the one with the black gloves. He kicked him and beat him right there at the doorstep.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Did -- did you notice whether the -- whether anything was being removed from your side of the house at that point in time?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes. When I was waiting for my husband, I saw that there was a truck in front of the house and they had loaded it with television-sets, heaters, some other equipment, computers, whatever they could find there. It was not a very big truck.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Where did that equipment come from? Was it your equipment? Did it belong to the OSCE? What was it?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Some was -- some were our equipment, such as the heaters, for example. But the others were OSCE's, such as the computers.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honours, we have -- I can sort of go into the next series of events, but we could also break at this point although we are a little bit early. I don't know what Your Honours prefer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Ms. Berisha, we have to interrupt now for lunchtime, and we will resume again at 2.00. So you can leave the courtroom and return, please, for 2.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, should we remind the witness that during the break she cannot speak to others. I don't remember whether she has been told that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We'll deal with that if it arises later, Mr. Marcussen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So the court will resume at 2.00. --- Luncheon recess taken at 12.28 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: With reference to the Witness K83, the Trial Chamber has decided that the particular circumstances affecting this witness do merit the requirement of the log, and therefore that will be incorporated into the written order which will be issued as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It's been explained to me for reasons which do not appear to be the fault of the witness she's just arrived back in the building this minute, so she should be with us shortly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Ms. Berisha, your evidence will now continue. Mr. Marcussen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Madam Berisha.

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I'm sorry you had to be pulled in to the courtroom this way. There seems to have been a mistake. It's not being held against you. Madam Berisha, I'd like to ask you -- we spoke about the 25th of March, 1999, before we stopped. You have explained that you handed some money over, a thousand Deutschemarks I think you said, to the policemen -- to one of the policemen who came to your house that day. Did anybody else give money to the police that day?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes. Later on I gave him money. As well I had some on my chest because they said to my husband: You either give us money or else look at our tank. It's in front of your house and we will blow up the place.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Apart from you, did anybody else give money to the police?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes. When my husband told me that they were asking for money, I gave the money that I had and my sister-in-law also had some money in her chest and she gave him this money as well just to be safe. But as she was trying to pull out the money, the policeman went and put his hands into her chest and took the money himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And you say the policeman, which policeman was that?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: The policeman with the black gloves.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And you mentioned that you were being threatened with a tank that would shell your house. Had you seen that --

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Had you seen a tank in the vicinity of your house that day?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes, I had seen it before when they came and took my husband, when the policeman with the knives ran towards my direction. This is when I saw it. It was opposite the house of Agron Berisha.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: May I ask that we get P189, page 1 up on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: While we wait for that to come up, could you describe the tank for me. What colour did it have?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. It was kind of green colour, green-grey colour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And how -- why do you say it was a tank? Could you try to describe how the vehicle you saw as a tank, how did that look?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: It was made of metal. It had big tires. It -- the tires were made of rubber and smaller, not that big as some of the bigger tanks, and it had the cannon in front. I don't -- I don't know the correct name. Maybe it's not a tank, maybe it's a Pinzgauer. I don't know really.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: But you saw it had wheels?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Now, on the picture you have on the screen, the location -- can you see the location of the tank on this picture? Or is it outside the picture?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: The tank was here, approximately, near our house, in line with Agron's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: The usher has given you a pen, and if you could ...

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Approximately it was here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: So it was on the road in front of your house where you have made a dot now?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes, on the road in front of my house, in front of Agron's house actually because it's here approximately, the location where it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Could I ask you to write an A, like alpha, next to the dot you just made so we can identify it later.

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you. How long did you -- do you think the police stayed all in all that day at your house?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Well, I don't know exactly. They did stay but not that long.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: After they had left, did you stay in the house -- in your own house?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: No. We were very scared, and we went to the house of my uncle -- to my husband's uncle, Vesel Berisha, which is just behind our house.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Is that the house that has number 2 on the picture you can see?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And the house where -- where your uncle lived, number 2 on the map, who lived on that house?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Sedat and his family lived in this house, so with his wife and his three children, then his brother Bujar with his wife and three children, his other brother Nexhmedin with his wife and his mother and father.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: So if we look at the family-tree again, would that be people who are in the upper right-hand quarter of the family-tree?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: So did you spend the night in Vesel's house?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes. My entire family and Vesel's -- Uncle Vesel's family spent the night together there. In total, we were 25.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: So are they -- the people that are marked with a colour in the upper row of the family-tree, you were all there. Is that correct? Except for Arben and Ismet and Faik and Bahrije and Vesel himself, but the people who that have the colour were there. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Those with -- in red and in blue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I'd like to move on to the next day, the 26th of March, 1999. In the morning of the 26th, did you see any -- did you see any heavy equipment belonging to either the police or the military in the vicinity of your house?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: What did you see?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Throughout the day you could see vehicles, policemen. We were always -- we always wanted to escape, but we couldn't because of this large movement. Behind the house, there were two tanks, big tanks, situated just above our houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Now, let's first deal with where those tanks were. Now, if we look again at the photograph you have on the screen, were the tanks located at a place you can see in the photograph or outside the photograph?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: You cannot see it here. It's much more behind.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: "Behind" meaning what direction? Up -- up, above the numbers?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: They are behind number 1 and 2. You cannot see the location where they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Approximately how far do you think they were away, the tanks, when you saw them?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: I don't know how far it is, but there were no more houses there. It was like a forest. There are no houses in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: The terrain there, is it flat or does it go -- is it a hill that go up or down behind the house?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Behind the houses it is like a hill, and further up it's a mountain, it's a forest.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And so tanks were up on the hill somewhere up behind the house. Is that how I should understand it?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Now, you described these as tanks. What colour were they, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, they were green, green-grey colour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And when you described them as tanks you said they were big -- they were very big. Did they look different from the one you had seen the day before?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes. The one that was in front of the house had rubber tires, while these had chains and were much bigger.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Could you -- they had -- the -- I don't think it came through in the translation how you described what they had instead of wheels. Could you try to describe that again, please?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes, yes. This is what I said. They did not have rubber tires, but they had chains.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you. And did they have a cannon?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: What direction was that -- the cannon of the tanks pointing?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: It was pointing towards our houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And approximately when was this? Was it in the morning, in the afternoon, middle of the day, that you saw them first time?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: I saw them at approximately 10.00 or 10.30 while I, with my youngest son, went from Sedat's house to Agron's mother.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: On that day did the police come to your house again?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: The policemen came to the house, to Sedat's house, where we were with our families.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: When did they come?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: At around noon, at around 12.00, 12.20.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Did you see them arrive?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes. I was in the sitting room together with the others. They came out of the police station, which is -- which can be seen from the house, it's in the direction of the house. When they came out of the police station, they ran. There were a lot of them, they were wearing uniforms and carrying automatic rifles. They first went to Ismet Kuci's house and from there they came to the place where we were staying.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And Ismet's house, is that on the photograph?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes, this one here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Does it have a number? Has it been marked with a number?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: No. The one numbered is the house of Ahmet Berisha.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Number 3 --

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: You cannot see all of the house on this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Okay. How many policemen do you think you saw?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: I don't remember now, but there were a lot. Too many.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Were -- you said they were wearing uniforms. Were they all wearing the same uniform or did they have different uniforms, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: No, they were not all of them wearing the same uniform. I don't remember them very clearly at the moment, but I know that they were wearing uniforms.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Marcussen, which house was pointed out as Ismet Kuci's house?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: That has not been marked. We can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, it's obviously one that is on the edge of the picture. Is it one on the right or one on the left?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Would you please take --

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: On the right -- to the right of my house.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Would you write, please -- you have been given the pen. Would you put a B on Ismet's house, please.

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Approximately it's here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: So it's outside or just at the border of the picture. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Okay. So you saw the police. You saw them come running. There were a lot of them coming to -- towards the house. Among the people that came, were there also people who did not have a uniform on?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes, but a few. There were a few civilians who were not wearing uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Were those civilians armed, do you remember seeing that -- whether you saw that?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes, yes. They were armed, and all of them were running.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: How did you react when you saw that?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: I was very scared, we all were.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Did anybody give you anything to calm you down?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: I was very upset even from the night before when the policemen had taken my husband and beaten him up, so I nearly fainted. I had the feeling that I was going to faint, and Sedat gave me tranquillizers because he could see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Do you know what that tranquillizer was?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: No, I don't. I just know that he gave it to me and he gave me a glass of water. He said: Just drink this. You have to calm down a little bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And did that help?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: I don't know. I was very scared.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: The police that came, were they -- were they asking for anybody in particular?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: The moment they came, one of them called Bujar in Albanian, this person was Zoran. He spoke Albanian very well. He grew up with Albanians, he ate together with Albanians. Everyone in Suhareke knew him, so he called for Bujar in Albanian, and he was cursing in Albanian as much as he could.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Where were you and your family at that time?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: We were all together in the sitting room in the first floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: So when Zoran called for Bujar, did Bujar go out?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: No. Hava, Bujar's mother, went out and asked him: What do you want? And he shouted at her and told her to go back in. Let Bujar come out, he said.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Did you and your family remain in the living-room or did you go somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: No. All of us were there, inside.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And did you stay -- did you remain in the living-room or did you go to another part of the house?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: No, we all remained there, in that room.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And then what happened?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Hava went out. Zoran shouted at her and told her to go back in. He was asking for Bujar to come outside. He was saying that they were going to eliminate all the Albanians, they were going to kill all the Albanians. And when Bujar came out, as soon as they saw him they cursed him in Albanian, and I heard the gun-shots. And then --

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Could I -- so -- so Bujar got out of the building and you heard a shot. Where were you when you heard the shot?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Inside. We were in the living-room while Bujar went to the staircase and went out from the other entrance because the house had two entrances. We were here in this living-room, and this living-room had this entrance, while Bujar went through the corridor to the staircase and came outside on this side.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Can -- okay. Did the rest of you remain in the -- in the house or did you leave the house at that time?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: As soon as we heard the gun-shots, when Bujar went out, everybody just screamed, children, men, women, and we began to run, some barefoot, some with their shoes on. So we left the house, we went out in the courtyard. I heard Bujar's son telling his mother: Mom, they killed our father.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Sorry --

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Bujar was laying down in the balcony.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I'm just going to stop you for one moment. It looks like the marked version of the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It's being attended to. If you need to go back to it, we'll have to take action at that stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Well, we can also -- is it possible to make this an in-court exhibit at a later stage and then we can just continue with a clean copy if that's easier and we can get the number --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: A copy can be taken from the recording that's being made to replace it. Are you going to use this again with more markings?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: We might, depending on how things come out, get a few more markings, but we can get it on a new copy. I just wanted to keep the A and the B.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, arrangements are being made to photocopy -- or to take a photograph of the one that's disappeared and it will be given an IC number once that arrangement has been made.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Wait until it's available. Don't give numbers to non-existent exhibits. We'll wait until we know it's available and then it will be given a number. You can meanwhile carry on, Mr. Marcussen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I'm sorry for the interruption. The -- so you were all leaving the building. Did you see Bujar after he had been shot yourself?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: As you were running out of the house, did you -- did you see anybody you recognised among the policemen?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: The policeman who I recognised was Zoran. I recognised Zoran at that moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Later on did you recognise anybody else?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Well, we were running in the direction of our house. We passed near Agron's house, and when we arrived here in front of the house I stopped there with my children and with Sedat's daughter, Dafina. And the first person that I recognised there was Miskovic. He was wearing a civilian uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now, could I ask you to take the pen again -- or you will be given the pen again. Now Agron's house, which one is this on the photograph?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: This one here is Agron's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: So that's the one that's marked with a number 5, is that --

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... now you said you --

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: -- you stopped with your daughter -- you stopped with your daughter and then you saw the man you referred to as Miskovic. Where is that on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Here is where I stopped with my four children and Dafina, Sedat's daughter. This is where we were, while here Miskovic -- while here I remember this was where Miskovic had taken my husband. At the same time, somebody else took Faton. I don't know who that was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Could I -- we need just to mark this so we remember it when we get to this later on. Now, the place that you stopped, would you mark that with an A, please. If you could just write A underneath or next to where you stopped.

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Okay. That became an A, yeah. And where you saw Miskovic, could you mark that with a B, please.

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And so you said that Miskovic had -- was with your husband. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes. And I could hear very well when he was shouting at my husband. He told him: Raise your hands. Up with your hands. And he shot him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: He cursed my husband and shot him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And you said you saw somebody grab on to Faton. Was that at approximately the same location?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Another policeman took Faton, but in the meantime Faton's mother was with Faton and she grabbed her son's hand and told him: Don't take my son. I'll come instead of him. At the same time there were several other policemen on this side and some civilians, and they also were shouting.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Okay. I think we will -- we can stop with the markings for a little bit. Did you also see Nexhmedin and Sedat?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: I remember Sedat. It's here where the policeman took them. And Sedat was trying to go towards Agron's house. I think he was trying to escape. I remember it very well when a police grabbed him by the arm and asked him: Where are you going? And he said: I'm going to have a look at Bujar. And from that moment on, I did not see Sedat anymore.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you were standing at -- at the point that you marked before with A. The people that had come out of the house, I understand they were running. What direction were they running in?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: The people who were leaving the house -- I can't remember. I did not see anyone. I remember my children and Dafina, and when the policeman shot Nexhat my daughter screamed. She screamed so loud that I think the whole of Suhareke could hear her. I did not see the other people, where they were running to.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Did your children run away from your house?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: At that moment, Nexhmedin and Lirije were holding hands. Lirije was Nexhmedin's wife. She was pregnant. She was only two weeks from her due date, and they were holding hands when we heard the shout: Shoot at them, shoot at them, and I did not see Nexhmedin anymore with Lirije. And when I saw that he had fallen down, I told my children: Escape because they will kill us all. It was Altin, my son, I was holding his hand while Majlinda and Redon, the younger one, Majlinda was holding him. Herolinda was going in another direction and I ran after her. So we divided into two groups, me and my children.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Okay. So the children that did not stay with you, what direction did they move in?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: My children, I know that they went in this direction, while myself and my daughter, we went to the -- towards the bus station, the police station, while my other daughter with my two sons and Dafina went to the other side.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: So your children went down in the direction of the number 6?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And you yourself went in the direction of the arrows going down -- downwards and in front of the buses and then horizontally on the map. Is that --

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Let's make this one an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That would be IC45, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Do you have the other one yet available?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Could we see page 3 of this same exhibit, please. Here we are. So this is -- now, that's an interesting thing. There seems to be some markings floating there from the last one. Are they kept on the previous --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It's now clear, so you can carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Madam Berisha, there's something marked with a number 1 up in the right-hand corner. What is that? A building.

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: I can only see number 2. Oh, yes, yes, I apologise. Now I can see number 1 as well. Number 2 is the police station. I apologise, number 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Number 1 is the police station. Thank you. And --

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: So when you started to run past the bus station, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: From the bus station towards the] Petrol station. At the petrol station Jashar Berisha asked me: What's the problem? What's the matter, Nexhat's wife? I told him: Uncle Jashar, all the men were killed. And I was running as fast as I can -- as I could. And when I came to this direction, I saw my daughter Herolinda, she was before me, and I saw the whole family that had gathered together.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Where did -- where had the family gathered?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: The family had gathered in front of a coffee shop here, approximately here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Is the coffee shop, is there a line going down to approximately where the coffee shop was and is it attached to a number on the picture?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes, number 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Did you speak to anybody from your family when you went to the coffee shop?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes, of course I spoke.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Who did you first speak to?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: First of all, I spoke with Avdija, Avdi Berisha, and I asked him: Why have you gathered here, why did you stop? And he told me that the police told them to stay there, and he didn't say anything else. He just kept his head down.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Did you see any police there at that time?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: No. When I went there where the whole family was, there were no policemen in the beginning. Majlinda came later with Altin and Dafina. And Altin was very pale in his face and he told me: Mom, I've been wounded, I've been wounded on my hand. At that time Lirije came, Nexhmedin's wife, and she said to me: Come, please come, because Uncle Nexhat is wounded and he is asking for you to go and help him. She told the same thing to Hava, her mother-in-law: Come, please, because Nexhmedin is dying and we need to help them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Hava and Lirije went together. I told Lirije: I can't. I don't want them to kill me and I don't want my children to remain without a mother and a father, and I did not go.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Did you go inside the coffee shop?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes. At that moment when I was speaking with Lirije, lots of policemen came and they ordered us to go inside the coffee shop.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Apart from the part of the Berisha family that you were from and Vesel's family, were there members of any other branches of the Berisha family in the coffee shop at that time?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes, there were others by the Berisha surname --

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Other -- for example, the families of Vesel and Sofije Berisha, is that right, as you've indicated on the family-tree?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Vesel's and Sofije's family. Avdi's family, Musli's family, and Hamdi's family.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And you have indicated on the family-tree in blue which parts of the family you remember -- of that side of the family you remember seeing at the coffee shop - is that correct - down at the bottom?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And you mentioned Avdi. Did he had any of his relatives with him?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Who --

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: His wife, his son, his brothers.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: You -- you were inside the coffee shop. What happened then?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: When we were ordered to go in, they also told us to sit down. We sat down, and they started shooting.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... see who was shooting?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: The Serb policemen were shooting.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: From where you were, could you see them or are you inferring from the people you saw around the place before that it was the police?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: I saw the policemen when they ordered us to go inside. And when we went inside, they started shooting.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm -- we can go into the events in more detail if you would like me to put more evidence about who in the coffee shop, what happened, but the witness has accepted this exhibit. So maybe we can move on without going into those details. I think it's difficult for the witness, so I'm seeking your guidance on what Your Honours would need.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, is her experience of what happened confined to shooting?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Well, I can clarify that with my -- with the witness. I understand that there were also grenades thrown --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, I'm only looking at the summary you've given us. Is it not of some importance to establish what weaponry was used? That's quite different from the detail of the consequences.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Yeah, let's cover that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Apart from shooting, did you hear any explosions in the coffee shop?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes. They also threw something and they exploded and people died. After they shot with their automatic rifles, they threw something. But I don't know what exactly that was; it just exploded.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Did they do that once or several times?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Twice. Whenever they saw anybody that was still alive, they threw those things in.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And between they threw these things in, were there shooting?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes. I think they were grenades that they threw in because the shrapnel from the grenade that they threw in was taken out of my abdomen at the hospital. I'm not sure exactly what kind of explosive that was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And if you are able to describe the -- the shooting, do you think it came from automatic weapons or are you able to describe the kind of shooting you heard?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: In the beginning they shot with automatic guns. I'm not -- I don't know what kinds of weapons they are, but I know the second time when they saw that I was alive they shot at me again. It took -- the bullet went into my shoulder and it was my luck that I remained alive.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Marcussen, how many survivors were there?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: My understanding is there was the witness and two others.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah. Now, if what you're -- you seek to avoid going into detail on is the victims, then I don't think we require you to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: That is indeed what I am -- I think it was a fairly gruesome scene and the witness's children were there and close relatives. So I think that's very difficult to talk about, so we would be happy not to go into that too much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Madam Berisha, when -- when the shooting eventually stopped, did anybody come into the shop?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes. The people who entered the shop were speaking in Serbian: We have to load these into -- on to the truck. We don't need these people here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Did you see the people who got into the shop or were you not looking at them?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: No, I didn't see them. I was lying on my stomach. I was pretending I was dead because when they thought somebody was alive, when they were lifting them up, they shot them. Even my son, when they lifted him up, they saw that he was alive, they shot him there and then. Only Gramoz, they could not -- did not see that he was alive, and that was his luck, his destiny, to remain alive. And Vjollca and me, they did not see that we were alive.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: So Vjollca and Gramoz are the names of the other two survivors apart from the witness. They are -- on the family-tree they are part of the family of Vesel and Hava Berisha up on the top right-hand side of the Exhibit P2346.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: The bodies that were taken out of the -- of the coffee shop, where were they taken?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: So we were loaded on the truck and the truck went in the direction of Prizren. Where I was speaking about Vjollca, Vjollca noticed that I was alive and she spoke to me and she said: Only Gramoz is alive. And at that time, thinking that maybe I would be able to find my husband alive, I said to Vjollca: Shall we jump off? And we need to tell what these policemen, the Serb policemen, did to our family only because we were Albanians. I jumped off first and then Vjollca came behind me. And somebody on the road took me, picked me up.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: I don't know where the truck went.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Excuse me one minute.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Do you know what happened to Gramoz? Did he also jump off; do you know?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes, he did. So after me, it was Vjollca and Gramoz that jumped off. So only us three are alive, where the rest we don't even know where their bones are lying, where their bodies are lying now, with the exception of the men and Fatime.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I'm not having an awful lot of questions left for you. But before we move on to what happened to you after you had jumped off.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I'd like to call up Exhibit 2344, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And while we're waiting for that to come up, Madam Berisha, when you spoke to -- you gave a statement to the Office of the Prosecutor in March of this year. And while you were here you were also shown a number of photographs of -- of different people and you were asked whether you could -- whether you knew the people on the photograph. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes. These are from the Berisha family, but I don't know all their names.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And an investigator noted down whether you knew the name of the person on the picture and whether or not you remembered seeing that person in the coffee shop. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: You already said that this -- this person you're not sure the name of the person, but you know this person to be a member of the Berisha family. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: What part of the Berisha family?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: This is Avdi Berisha's family, that part of the family. In fact, Avdi's brothers.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And so that is -- on the family-tree it's someone from the mid-row of the family-tree. Avdi is in middle -- the middle family, so it's somebody at the --

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes, Saiti and Hanumsha family-tree

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And the girl we see in this picture, do you remember seeing her in the coffee shop. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Could we go to the next page of the exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: The same question: Do you know who this is?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes. This was Avdi's mother.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Avdi's mother, okay. Was she at the coffee shop?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes, yes, she was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And if we could go to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: The girl we see on this picture, was she a member of the Berisha family, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes. She also is a daughter of the old lady's sons, one of those.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And do you remember her at the coffee shop?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... the last page of this exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: This gentleman, do you know who he is?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes. This is Avdi's brother, his elder brother, Musli Berisha.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And do you remember seeing him in the coffee shop?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Now I'd also like if we can show Exhibit 117, page 1, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Ms. Berisha, was the older lady in the photograph Hanumsha?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it was Hanumsha. I don't know her name. I am not sure --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- about the names.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I should maybe explain. We have this continued scanning and printing process of these photographs do make them lose quality. We have another version of these photographs in e-court and they will be shown to another witness later on. It's quite clear that they are the same photographs, but what we see in e-court is not the best quality. Sorry, maybe we should go to page number 2. Okay. Can we zoom in on the bottom one first, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Do you recognise this place?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes, this is the coffee shop that the Serb police ordered us to be in.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And can we go up and look at the other one of these pictures, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And this?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes, this is where Dafina was, Vjollca's daughter. This is where my second daughter was, this is where my elderly was daughter, where Avdi and his wife Lirije were.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you. I don't think we need to make markings on the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: But clearly the witness is indicating where various people were on this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Okay. We'll go back to where we took off before we started to look at these photographs again. You jumped off the truck. Do you know the name of where you got off the truck or jumped off the truck?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Not at the very moment, I didn't, but from the people who picked me up I learned that I jumped off at the village of Malasia e Re. It's on the road to Prizren.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: The road to Prizren where?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: From Suhareke to Prizren.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you. We will jump somewhat quickly for what -- from here on out. Did you receive treatment for your injuries after you had gotten off the truck?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes. I was taken to Grejkoc village, but they didn't have much medicine to treat me. They administered IV. I had some stitches on my arm. It was done with an ordinary thread, but I was told that they had to do it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: How many wounds had you sustained? You told us already that you had been shot in the shoulder and that a shrapnel had been taken out of your abdomen. Did you receive other wounds?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes. On the shoulder the bullet went through my shoulder. Also on my leg in the right-hand side of the leg, and the exit wound was on the other side. And my back is full of shrapnels, small pieces of grenades, same with my stomach. I had wounds all over my body.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you. Are you saying the shrapnels are still there, they have not been removed?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: How long did you stay -- how long did you stay in Kosovo after this?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: One month. I stayed for one month in Kosova in the mountains, wounded, and there I saw all sorts of things. And I don't think books and computers can memorise everything that I've seen with my own eyes, everything that I went through. I've seen children dying, young girls dying. I seen my cousin, my uncle's daughter, who went crazy and many, many other things.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Let's talk about the day you left Kosovo. Approximately when did you leave Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: I remember it very well. I think it was the 6th of May. From the village of Vraniq we went to Sopija village. There there was a Serb, a different Serb, who was dressed in uniform. He stopped my father and asked: Where are you going? We were all in tractors. And my father answered just by raising his hands in the air and saying just: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Sorry --

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: And he just said to my father: If you come back, we will kill you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: The man who was in a uniform, what kind of uniform was that? What was the colour, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: I don't remember now but he was old. He was not young. He was about 55 years old, I would say. He was wearing a uniform - that I know - but I don't know the colour of the uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you. Did -- were you -- were anybody asked to pay any money from your family?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: From Vraniq when we arrived at Bukoshi school, there was hassle there as well. I was in a very bad condition. There were a lot of Serbs, some in uniforms, some without uniforms. They stopped our tractors. They separated the women and placed them in the school building, and then the women told us that they had taken all the valuables from them. They took the men and they never returned them. They took my uncle and some elderly persons. After a few hours, they released the elderly persons, but not the men.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
