utterances.text: Where did you cross into Albania? Do you know the name of the place where you crossed over the border?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: In Kukes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Okay. Before you left Albania, was anything taken away from you and the other people in the convoy?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: The same thing happened when we came at the border. The policemen were with automatic rifles pointed at us and asked for money, for gold. And they said: We will get our automatic rifles ready and to shoot you, and the women gave them everything they had from the valuables. And then they allowed us to cross the border and get into Albania.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: You described the people who did this as being policemen. Why do you say that?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: They were wearing uniforms, all of them, at the border.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: These particular men, do you remember the uniform they were wearing or just that they were wearing a uniform?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Well, now I don't remember the colour of the uniform. Many years have passed and my head is not what it used to be. I just remember that they had uniforms on and that they were carrying automatic rifles and that they were very aggressive.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: What about your identity papers, were you allowed to take them with you to Albania?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes. They asked for identity documents. I didn't have anything with me. But, yes, they did ask for identity documents, and who had them with them they submitted the documents to the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And were they given the identity papers back or not?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: No, never. They would take your life let alone identity cards.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Okay. After these events you stayed in Albania for a while, I understand. And --

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And you were -- were you interviewed by the OSCE; do you remember?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And you were -- you were also interviewed by the Office of the Prosecutor of this Tribunal. Did you at some point in time give a blood sample?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And who did you give that blood sample to, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: To the Tribunal, to The Hague Tribunal. When I went to have this operation in Albania, to have this shrapnel removed from my stomach, I know that they took some blood from me. But later on, I know that blood samples were taken by The Hague Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honours, for now that concludes my questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Marcussen. Mr. O'Sullivan.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, the order will be: General Lukic, General Pavkovic, General Ojdanic, General Lazarevic, Mr. Sainovic, and Mr. Milutinovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mrs. Berisha. My name is Branko Lukic. I will ask you to find some more strength in you, if you can, please, to help us clarify some remaining matters. In my questioning I will jump from one point to another. It will not be following a narrative like the Prosecutors did. So I will mention to you certain dates, in relation to which I will have some questions. When you mentioned that the OSCE arrived in Suva Reka in 1998 and stayed at the Boss Hotel in Shiroko, did the owner of that hotel have the name of Miskovic, just was it the same man as the one who later participated in the killing of your family?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Are you aware that because of that fact people from the OSCE moved to your house? Were you afraid that some of them -- is it because of that fact that they moved from that hotel to your house, is it because of that that this man bore a grudge against your family?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: The OSCE came, moved to our house out of their free will. They did not come there to protect us.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I see there was some misunderstanding by interpreters, both into English and into Albanian. Maybe my question was not phrased in the happiest possible way. Are you aware that the owner of the Boss Hotel had quarrelled with or attacked your husband or any other member of your family because OSCE staff had moved from his hotel to your house?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: I don't know that. Ask him. He should know. My husband didn't tell me anything, but he must know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Already on the 24th of March, 1999, lootings began in Suva Reka. For instance, the house of Murat Suka was looted. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I heard. Personally, I didn't see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At that moment, was Murat Suka at his home; do you know?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is that a convenient place to interrupt you, Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Ms. Berisha, we need another break, and that will be for half an hour. So could you now please leave the courtroom, and we will see you again at 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And we'll adjourn now until 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Berisha, can we continue?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When I asked you about the looting of the house of Murat Suka, we heard that you hadn't been there and you had not been present. Do you know if OSCE property was stolen or his personal property was stolen?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: I don't know. I only know what I was told that people entered, broke into his house, and stole things from his house.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When you were informed that some people had inquired -- or rather, the former OSCE guard inquired about their copier machine, that was suspicious to you, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: I don't understand. What suspicion are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were you afraid that you may be looted, that OSCE property from your house may be looted?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: They didn't ask me about the copier machine, they asked my husband. The guard, Miskovic's brother, asked my husband about this, not me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In your statement you said it sounded suspicious to you. That's why I asked that question, where you were suspicious because you were afraid that your house may be looted or for some other reason.

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: As I said, he didn't ask me, he asked my husband. But of course we were scared. Whenever we would hear that they were breaking into houses, we were scared.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I will take you back for a moment to this person Miskovic whom we discussed before. Do you know that his house had been hit a month before these events from a hand-held rocket-launcher?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When you speak about the 25th of March, 1999, in your statement, you say that you did not recognise any of those people and that you believe they were not policemen from Suva Reka. Paragraph 3 on page 4 on the English version; and page 5, paragraph 2 in Albanian; and paragraph 4, page 4 in B/C/S. Is it correct that you did not recognise any of those policemen?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: No. On that day when these policemen came early in the morning, I didn't recognise any of them. However, later on my daughter who was upstairs in the living room, she said to me: Mom, this is the policeman that I told my grandpa about. She always told my father about this policeman who would get on the bus and travel from Mushtisht to Suhareke. So this is what my daughter told me, but personally I didn't recognise him.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So you, yourself, do not know to which unit these men belonged?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: No, I don't. As for this policeman that I mentioned, I only heard of him through my daughter, when she said that this is the policeman from Mushtisht. Personally, I didn't know him, my father did.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In your statement, English version page 7, paragraph 1; Albanian version page 9, paragraph 1; and B/C/S version page 7, paragraph 2 you say that you wanted to leave the house of Vesel Berisha but you were not able to because of the shooting. Is it true that that night gun-fire lasted all night -- or rather, there was fighting on the slopes around the town between Serb forces and the KLA, specifically in the direction of Rastane and Pecane?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: No, I did not mention the KLA or Rashtane [phoen] or Peqan. What I said is true. There was gun-fire heard throughout the night. This has nothing to do with the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Ma'am, do you know - and if you don't you can say so - that there was fighting on the 25th of March, 1999, in Rastane between the KLA and Serbian forces?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: No, I don't know. I was in my house with my family.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In your statement, English version page 7, paragraph 5; Albanian, page 9, last paragraph; B/C/S, page 7, last paragraph you describe Zoran and you say that he spoke fluent Albanian and that he was a driver of an Albanian bus. Do you know that he used to work at the petrol station, a job where he was later replaced by Jashar Berisha?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now I just want to ask you, when you talk about that incident wherein people were running towards your house, and in your statement, Albanian version paragraph 3 on page 9; Albanian page 7, paragraph 3 -- sorry, English version page 7, paragraph 3 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, let me stop you for a moment. We're not working from this statement, as you know, as it would be much easier if you just asked your questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay, I'll do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And if you have to challenge the witness by use of the statement, then go back to it. But this is just using a lot of words that don't --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: -- assist, I think, and probably not using your time to best advantage.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You heard from Sedat's son Drilon that he said to his father: Look, there's Zoran in that group, the fat one. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sedat looked out the window and said: "They are all from Suva Reka. Zoran is there with his brother." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You are aware, thus, of the incident that happened when Serbian women protested and when an OSCE vehicle hit Vera Petrovic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: I did --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Please, Mrs. Berisha, Mr. Marcussen is objecting to that question, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Yes, I am, Your Honour. The witness was not asked about this in direct, and the Defence have not -- my learned colleague haven't indicated that he was going to use the statement. I think we're now getting out a little far from what this cross-examination should be about. We're outside the scope of the direct and she's being cross-examined on her witness statement which has not been notified to the Prosecution at the beginning of the testimony of the witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, the cross-examination isn't confined to the incidents that are raised in the direct examination, and it's not clear at the moment to me that the statement is a necessary prerequisite for asking this particular question. I don't think in fact that Mr. Lukic has referred to the statement. He's putting a point from his knowledge of the information that this witness can give him, which may or may not assist his case. And he's entitled to request questions of that nature. So carry on, please, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mrs. Berisha, you know about the incident when an OSCE vehicle injured Vera Petrovic, the mother of the same Zoran that we have mentioned before. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes, I heard about it but I did not see it myself. I just heard about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it the case that Miskovic and Zoran were the leaders when your family was assaulted and killed?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes. Because I could hear the shouts and Zoran's voice prevailed. I could hear Zoran's voice all the time, maybe because I knew him, that he was Zoran. I don't know. I don't know how to describe the scene, the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I just wish to ask you about one more point. When you were on the truck, the truck stopped and some woman outside the truck asked: Son, did you finish the job? Did you hear those words?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes, I heard those words.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: A male voice answered: Yes.

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The female voice said: Have a good trip.

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The voice sounded familiar to you and you thought at that moment that it was Laza's wife Vera, Zoran's mother?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: I thought it was -- that's what I thought, yes. I did not see her, but I heard the voice.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Vjollca recognised the voice. She told you: Did you hear this, it was Vera, Laza's wife?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Vjollca knows better, she knows better than me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But we may conclude that you both recognised Vera's voice on that occasion. Is it not the case?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes. I think it was Vera's voice, Zoran's mother.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Does that tell us that Vera knew in advance what was going to happen to your family?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: She knows that -- you can ask her about this. She would be able to tell you whether she knew or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just a second.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Also, at the moment when they were dragging you while you were injured, somebody said: Hurry up, hurry up, we have to clean up here?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that's what they said in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: May we then conclude that somebody wished to cover up this crime?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: You can ask them. Those Serbs know. They know because they committed the crime, they covered it up, and even today, seven years on, they're still hiding what -- and covering up what they did. You can ask them, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would only like to ask you this: At the moment when your house was being surrounded --

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: You can ask me whatever you want.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Just one more question. While your house was being surrounded, that group of men included civilians and gypsies. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes, yes, some of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were gypsies also in civilian clothes?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Yes, there were some. Yes, some gypsies and Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Aleksic -- oh, Mr. Ackerman, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Ms. Berisha, I just want to express our sympathy for what happened to you and your family and we have no questions of you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Sepenuk.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPENUK
utterances.text: No questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. O'Sullivan.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: No questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Marcussen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Just one question on one area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Ms. Berisha, Mr. Lukic asked you about the policemen that you testified in direct examination that you did not know and then the -- the policemen that you knew. Now, the policemen that came to your house on the 25th, did you know any of those policemen?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: On the 25th, I did not know or recognise any of them. My daughter said that that policeman was from Mushtisht. I did not know him, but for the past three months she had been travelling from Mushtisht to Suhareke and she recognised him. She told me that, that was a policeman from Mushtisht.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And -- but on the 26th, the people that came to your house on that day, among those were people you knew from Suva Reka. Is that what your evidence is?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: There were people I recognised, but I don't know their names. I knew Miskovic's name. He had civilian clothes. He wasn't wearing police uniform, but he had -- he was wearing all black. But also Zoran was there and Miskovic's brother was there, the one who formerly was a guard at our house.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Now, the other thing, Your Honours, I understand that it was not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Before you move on. Ms. Berisha, you said Miskovic had civilian clothes and then you said he was wearing all black. Do you mean black civilian clothes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, black civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Marcussen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I also -- sorry. I understand that it was not possible to recover the exhibit that was lost in cyberspace, so I suggest that we just re-create that exhibit. That should be a quick exercise. If we could see page 1 of Exhibit 189.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Ms. Berisha, you will remember that I asked you to indicate on this photograph the place where you saw the -- the vehicle that you described as a tank on the 25th and you put a mark A on this photograph. We have lost the image that you marked on, so could I ask you to indicate again where the tank was on the 25th.

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Approximately here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you. And on the same photograph you also indicated the location of a house and you marked a B. I think it was Ismet's house. Could I ask you to repeat where that was.

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Ismet's house cannot be seen here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Could you indicate --

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: It's on this side. It cannot be seen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Could you make a dot --

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: This is my husband's cousin's house, but that house cannot be seen here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Could you mark -- maybe make an arrow indicating the direction in which the house can be found.

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: Approximately in this direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's leave it at this. There's a dot in the upper right-hand side of the photograph, indicating the direction out of the picture where the house approximately is found.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I suggest we make this in-court exhibit something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be IC46, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: The Prosecution is finished with the re-direct, so we have no further questions for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CHOWHAN
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I have a question. This is from the Bench. I just wanted to understand what type of relationship you had with Miskovic, who was the owner of the Boss Hotel. Was there a strong enmity between you and them or the Berisha family because mainly the fact that you -- you asked the OSCE to transfer its headquarters to your premises and leave his hotel, which must be generating income for him. Was that the basic cause which created more enmity between your family and Miskovic -- I'm sorry if I'm not correctly -- pronouncing it correctly.

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: No, on the contrary. My husband's older brother was friends with Miskovic and Miskovic's brother. On the contrary, as I said. We never had any problems. We never had any problems with any of the Serbs there. Our men did not have any conflict or any problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CHOWHAN
utterances.text: So even after the shifting of the OSCE office to your premises, which must have caused him a loss, the relationship did not strain. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: SHYRETE BERISHA
utterances.text: There was no problem between us, no problem at all. I don't know -- I'm not aware of any.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Marcussen, is there any problem about identifying the present whereabouts of the witness and is that confidential?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I don't think it's any problem. The witness is not living in the region.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: But -- excuse me. We could ask the witness whether there would be any problem. I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wouldn't like to disclose that, but I can give it to you. I mean the information where I live. But I don't want the accused to know where I am living now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, that won't be necessary. Thank you. Well, Mrs. Berisha, that concludes your evidence. The Trial Chamber recognise the courage that it must have taken for you to come here and talk of these brutal events. We thank you for coming to give your evidence and confirm that you're now free to leave the court.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Marcussen, who is the next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, the next witness is K83. I don't know whether we need break -- yes, I see from the AV booth we would need a short 20-minute break to set up for that witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, we will break now while that is done and resume at five minutes to 5.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, I gather that for the witness to come in we have to have the blinds drawn, so let's do that. And can I clarify whether we have the same problem as we had before, that some of these screens can be seen from the public gallery?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is it only Mr. O'Sullivan's screen that's the problem?

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Well, if it is, we won't put the video on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So can you make sure you won't use the video part of the screen, and all the others should be facing away from the public gallery.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Closed session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The court is now set up so that your voice and your appearance cannot be recognised by the public, and that will be the case throughout your evidence. Could you now, therefore, make the solemn declaration to tell the truth by reading aloud the document which will be placed before you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated. Mr. Marcussen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Could the usher please show this document to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Sir, does that piece of paper contain a description of your identity, please? Just answer yes or no.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: If you would hand that back to the usher and the usher can give that to the Court.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: There's -- an electronic version of this has been uploaded into the e-court system and has P2352 as an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Sir, you -- after completing your primary school and secondary school, did you do your military service?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And after that did you start to work in factory in the town where you lived?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Were you at any point in time asked to join the police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: When approximately was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83
utterances.text: It was in 1993, after my military service was completed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honours, just sorry for interrupting, I should of course request that P2352 be placed under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, that will be done.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: In what capacity did you join the police, as a reserve policeman or as a full-time police officer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83
utterances.text: As a reserve police officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Were you issued a uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Could you describe that uniform to the Court, please. What was the colour?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83
utterances.text: Blue, camouflage work uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Were you also issued a weapon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83
utterances.text: Yes, I was issued a weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: In the beginning, how often did you -- were you on duty as a police officer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83
utterances.text: Well, two or three months. It depended on the situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Is that once every two or three months or are we -- does that mean -- so that means you were on duty once every two or three months?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83
utterances.text: Well, I would work for six months or three months. It depended.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Did you get to be on duty more from 1998?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83
utterances.text: 1998, the entire year, all the way up to the war in 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Were you working full time during that period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Why was there that increase in your duty as a police officer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83
utterances.text: Because there was a labour shortage, if I can put it that way, in the police force.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: What was that labour shortage due to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83
utterances.text: Because active-duty policemen were leaving their jobs for the most part; they didn't want to work.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Do you know why they left?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83
utterances.text: Well, they were afraid that they would get killed during the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Could you describe what kind of duty you did when you were on work as a police officer.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83
utterances.text: Well, while I was on the police force we would have guard duty in front of the SUP building. Then we would carry food, water, ammunition for patrols, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: When you were on patrol, did you patrol in Suva Reka town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83
utterances.text: Suva Reka and the surrounding villages of the municipality of Suva Reka.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: While you were serving in Suva Reka town, were there any -- were there any armed conflict there, meaning battles?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: In the town of Suva Reka or elsewhere in the municipality?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83
utterances.text: In the town itself and in the surrounding area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Where did the battle in Suva Reka town take place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83
utterances.text: Well, from the SUP building it's on the road leading to Rastane, so it's 3 kilometres away from Suva Reka.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: How far from the SUP building were the battles taking place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83
utterances.text: 3 to 5 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: So is it correct to say that there were no battles in the inner city of Suva Reka, in the area of the post office and the municipal building and in that area, the market?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Sorry, is it not correct to say that or is it that there were no battles in that area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83
utterances.text: No battles. No battles in the centre, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: In what areas outside of Suva Reka did you go on patrol in 1998 and 1999?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83
utterances.text: The village of Movljane, Samodreza, Musutiste, and the surrounding villages. I can't remember now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Were there any incidents of terrorist attacks on -- on people on the roads outside Suva Reka?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83
utterances.text: I did not understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Outside Suva Reka town itself, were there incidents where there were terrorist attacks on people moving on the roads?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And so when you -- and had the police set up check-points along the roads to try to control that situation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83
utterances.text: Yes, there were some check-points.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And you mentioned earlier that you were supplying -- supplying units outside Suva Reka town with food and other supplies. Were those the kind of places that you would be going to with supplies?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: In 1998 or 1999, did -- was the police force in Suva Reka reinforced by police forces coming from the outside?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Reinforcements came from other towns in Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Do you know what units came to your area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83
utterances.text: Well, members of the police force came and of the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Were they stationed in Suva Reka town or in other places?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83
utterances.text: Some were in town, and the rest were in the surrounding villages, the villages surrounding Suva Reka.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you. I'll now ask you a bit about the SUP in Suva Reka. Who was at the head of the SUP in Suva Reka?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83
utterances.text: At the head of the SUP of Suva Reka was Repanovic, Radojko, the commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Who was the commander of the police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83
utterances.text: The commander of the police was Repanovic, Radojko.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: What was the name of his deputy?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83
utterances.text: Dragan Borisavljevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Was there an officer called Vitosevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83
utterances.text: Vitosevic was the head of the SUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: At the SUP station, was there also some officers from the DB, state security?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Could you tell us the names of those officers, if you know, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83
utterances.text: Misko Nisevic and Milan Jablanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Was there also an Albanian employed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83
utterances.text: There was an Albanian, Iljaz. I cannot remember his last name now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Misko --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So, Mr. Marcussen, do we have two heads or am I misreading this? We've got Repanovic and we've got Vitosevic, or Vitosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Let's clarify that with the witness before I try to assist.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Vitosevic, how would you describe his functions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83
utterances.text: Vitosevic was the head of the SUP, that is to say that he was in charge of civilians who worked on identity papers, passports, traffic licenses, registration of vehicles, and so on and so forth. And the commander was just for the police, those who were in uniform, the uniformed police.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: So is it correct to say that Vitosevic was the head of the entire police station and Repanovic was the head of the police force as such?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Sir, you mentioned Misko Nisevic. Apart from --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Did he also own a hotel in town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83
utterances.text: Yes, he had a hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: What was the name of that hotel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83
utterances.text: The Boss Hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like to go into -- sorry, before I do that. What was the name of your commander, your immediate superior in other words.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83
utterances.text: Nenad Jovanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I would like to now take you -- talk about an event -- some events that occurred after the beginning of the NATO bombing. It is the 26th of March. Do you remember that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Were you on work -- were you on duty that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Where were you in the morning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83
utterances.text: In the morning five of us were out on the ground. We wanted to take water, food, ammunition to the members of our police force who were out in the field, that is to say ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Sir, you had been out in the field. Where had you been?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83
utterances.text: Djinovci. That was the name of the place, Djinovci.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you. Who were with you on that patrol?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83
utterances.text: Nenad Jovanovic, the assistant commander, then Radovan Tanovic, Sladjan Cukaric, Miki Petkovic, and I.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Approximately at what time did you come back from the patrol?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83
utterances.text: Well, approximately say after half an hour or an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: What time of the day was it, morning, afternoon, noon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83
utterances.text: Morning, morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: When you came back, did you see any police units that were not normally in Suva Reka?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83
utterances.text: I didn't understand you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: When you came back from your patrol, did you see anything in particular outside the SUP?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: What was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83
utterances.text: Well, there were two trucks there that -- well, policemen were getting out and these were armoured trucks. And policemen were walking out of these trucks.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And those trucks, were they normally stationed in -- in Suva Reka?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Do you know what unit those policemen were from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83
utterances.text: I just know that Cegar was their code. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: When you say "Cegar was their code," is that the way they were referred to on the radio?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes, right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Do you know that the Cegar call sign from the officer who was leading the policemen that you saw?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83
utterances.text: Cegar 1, Cegar Jedan.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: At the time did you know his name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83
utterances.text: I can't remember now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Have you -- have you -- have you later learned his name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: What is his name, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83
utterances.text: Mitrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Could you tell me how you learned his name was Mitrovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83
utterances.text: Through some colleagues who worked with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Have you ever been shown a picture of him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83
utterances.text: That was in 90 -- in 90 -- in 1997 -- no, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Who showed the pictures to you? I'm not so interested in the time, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83
utterances.text: Well, the gentleman from the police, from the DB, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Were you asked to identify Cegar 1 from a series of photographs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: How many photographs were there that you were shown when you were asked to identify him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83
utterances.text: There were five.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And did you manage to identify him as one of the five?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And when you identified Cegar 1, is that when you were told his name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Approximately how many police officers were with Cegar 1 on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83
utterances.text: Well, there were about 40. There must have been 40.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Were they wearing the same uniform as you were or were they wearing a different uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83
utterances.text: They had camouflage uniforms but military camouflage uniforms and camouflage vests, military ones. And it said "police" on the back, "policija."

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: If you remember, what colour was the uniform itself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K83
utterances.text: Green.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is that a convenient --

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is that a convenient time to interrupt you?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, sir, that -- we have to conclude the proceedings for this evening, and you will require to return tomorrow to continue with your evidence. We will resume at 9.00, so you will be here in time to continue your evidence at 9.00. Meanwhile, it is extremely important that you do not discuss any part of your evidence with any person whatsoever. And by that I mean either the evidence you've given already or the evidence you may yet give. Discuss anything else you wish this evening, but absolutely forbidden is any discussion of the evidence. You understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, please stay where you are just now until we rise and leave the court and then arrangements will be made for you also to leave the court, as they were made for you to come in. And we'll resume tomorrow at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
